title: Hom out of an extension by zero from a stratum
statement:
In the situation of [det-lem-formal-closed-support-derived], let
$u\colon S\hookrightarrow Z$ be an open immersion, $a=i\circ u\colon S\hookrightarrow X$,
and $a_!=i_*u_!$ (as in [sk-lem-coefficient-heart]). Let $L$ be a finite
locally projective $\Lambda_S$-module with dual
$L^\vee=\mathcal Hom_{\Lambda_S}(L,\Lambda_S)$. Then, naturally in
$K\in\D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$,

$$
R\operatorname{Hom}_X(a_!L,K)\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_Z(u_!L,R\underline\Gamma_ZK)
\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_S(L,u^*R\underline\Gamma_ZK)
\simeq R\Gamma\bigl(S,L^\vee\otimes u^*R\underline\Gamma_ZK\bigr).
$$

In particular $\Hom_{\D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)}(a_!L,K[q])=H^q(S,L^\vee\otimes u^*R\underline\Gamma_ZK)$
for every $q$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-proetale-finite-projective-dualizable] to L and reverse the resulting exact pairing by symmetry. The tensor-Hom adjunction and uniqueness of its right adjoint identify ihom L with tensorLeft of the internal dual stratumDual. Internal Hom, being a right adjoint, preserves finite limits. Transport this property across the displayed natural isomorphism to prove stratumDualTensor_preservesFiniteLimits.

For B=L-dual, exactness identifies the unary left derived functor of tensorLeft B with its termwise mapDerivedCategory. The cochain tensor with the single complex B[0] is naturally the termwise tensor functor. Descend this isomorphism to homotopy categories, use the unary left-derived property of tensor with Qh(B[0]), and uniqueness of left derived functors. The single/Q/Qh comparison then gives stratumDualTensor_derived. All comparison maps are existing localization and single-complex comparisons; no new resolution or tensor product is defined.

Set A=u_!L. The sheaf adjunction i_* ⊣ closedSupport from [det-lem-formal-closed-support-adjunction] identifies additive coyoneda from i_*A with closedSupport followed by additive coyoneda from A. Install closedSupport_lowerStarExact from the same adjunction module as a local finite-colimit-preservation instance. Together with the existing finite-limit preservation of lowerStar, Mathlib infers preservation of homology. Since i_* is exact, [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] says its right adjoint preserves K-injectives. Right-derive the natural isomorphism and apply the existing right-derived composition isomorphism. This gives the first comparison as a natural isomorphism of functors.

Similarly use exact u_! and its adjunction with u^* ([def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek], [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek-adjunction]). Its right adjoint preserves K-injectives. The exact upperStar functor is computed termwise on derived categories. Right-derived composition and the exact-functor comparison give the second natural isomorphism, and whiskering by derived closedSupport gives the required clause.

Choose a right dual of L from [lem-proetale-finite-projective-dualizable]. Braiding gives the opposite pairing, and uniqueness of right adjoints identifies ihom L with tensorLeft of its internal dual. Tensor with L is exact, so ihom L preserves K-injectives. The tensor-Hom adjunction evaluated at the unit, followed by the right unitor, identifies ihom L followed by Hom(unit,-) with Hom(L,-). Right-derived composition therefore identifies RHom(L,-) with derived sections after the exact dual tensor. Whisker by open restriction and closedSupport to obtain the third comparison.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-coyoneda-evaluation] to i_*u_!L and every integer q. It identifies shifted derived Hom with degree-q homology of stratumGlobalRHom. Compose the three already constructed natural isomorphisms and whisker by the homology functor. This gives the last clause, with no boundedness or constructibility restriction.

split_report.summary: Audited the imported three-isomorphism proof against the current basics blueprint. The item has no finished declaration in WeilConjectures. Replaced the under-cited imported steps with five complete steps: closed-support adjunction, exact open extension adjunction and K-injectives, finite-projective evaluation/K-flatness, derived internal Hom and global sections, and shifted-Hom naturality. No new DAG nodes were needed; the parallel smooth-purity node is recorded as same_as. Corrected the earlier attempt’s step 4 by distinguishing sheaf complexes from global-section complexes and citing the full K-injective definition of RΓ rather than inferring an isomorphism from cohomology groups. The a_! identity is the item’s own definition; the coefficient-heart result, whose coefficients and closure factorization are narrower, is not invoked as a theorem. Second reading made shift stability of K-injectives and the null-homotopy sign explicit, strengthened three truncated citation quotes to include their formulas, and independently searched Mathlib for the finite-free sheaf Hom formulation.
split_report.blueprint: First isomorphism: step 1; second isomorphism and K-injective restriction: step 2; finite-projective dual/tensor calculation: step 3; third isomorphism: step 4; naturality and final H^q formula: step 5.

tool_uses.why: Exactness of the pullback on the actual pulled-back condensed coefficient sheaves.
Existence of K-injective representatives on the small pro-etale ringed sites.
The exact left adjoint u_! implies u^* preserves K-injectives.
Global sections of the internal Hom are the ordinary Hom complexes in the finite-projective calculation.
Identifies the tensor product used in the evaluation map and its termwise complex.
Supplies the abelian sheaf-module setting and sectionwise kernels used in the direct-summand exactness argument.
Provides the K-flat notion used to justify ordinary tensor computing derived tensor.
Defines the derived internal Hom model used for the third isomorphism.
Makes the internal Hom complex K-injective when the first argument is K-flat.
Identifies derived global sections with ordinary sections on a K-injective representative.
Compares homotopy and derived morphisms into K-injective representatives.
Defines the Hom-complex differential used to identify shifted morphisms with degree-q cohomology.
Makes the ringed sites small in the fixed universe, as required for the generic unbounded K-injective results; this is a size convention, not a change of the unit route.
